title: RFC 7807 problem details as the error shape the client consumes
context: The client must render errors it can rely on structurally. The wire error shape is a whole-project decision shared with whatever serves the API; this ADR records the client half. A application-api-rest blueprint applied to the same project contributes its own decision on the same topic, and blueprint composition will surface that pairing for the operator to reconcile at add time. That surfacing is intended.
decision: The client treats RFC 7807 problem details (type, title, status, detail, instance, plus service extensions) as the canonical error shape. The data layer (TAC-204) normalises any non-conforming response into this shape at the boundary; UI code renders from the envelope, mapping fields to user-actionable copy per application-spa-REQ-017, and never parses ad-hoc error bodies.
consequences: Error rendering is uniform and specifiable. When the backend natively emits problem details the normaliser is a pass-through; when it does not, the normaliser is quarantine for the inconsistency. Composing with the application-api-rest blueprint raises a deliberate conflict on this topic; the expected resolution is one project-level ADR adopting RFC 7807 end to end.

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-endpoint error shapes
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Unverifiable error UX and blame-shaped fallback copy.

alternativesConsidered.name: Message-string-only errors
alternativesConsidered.summary: Reduce every failure to a string.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Loses status semantics and retry-ability the UX requirements need.
